memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Moses, "Say to the Israelites: 'Any man or woman who wrongs another in any way and so is unfaithful to the Lord is guilty and must confess the sin they have committed.'" - Num 5:5-7a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God addresses what happens when one person wrongs another. Notice the striking thing He says: to wrong another person is to be "unfaithful to the Lord." When we sin against people, we are also sinning against God Himself. There is no such thing as a purely "private" wrong that involves only the two people concerned.

This lifts our understanding of sin to a higher level. We often measure our wrongs by how they affect other people, and if no great harm seems done, we shrug them off. But every sin against a neighbour is also a sin against the God who made that neighbour in His image.

The remedy God gives begins with confession: "must confess the sin they have committed." Not excusing it, not hiding it, not blaming others — but honest confession. There is something deeply healing about naming our wrong for what it is, before God and before the person we have hurt.

King David understood this. After his great sin, he cried to God, "Against you, you only, have I sinned" (Ps 51:4) — knowing that his wrong reached all the way to heaven.

The New Testament assures us that "if we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us" (1 John 1:9). Honest confession is not the path to shame; it is the doorway to grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you see your wrongs against others as also against God?
- Is there a sin you need to honestly confess today?
- Do you tend to excuse and hide, or confess and turn?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me to see my sin honestly — not only how it affects others, but how it grieves You. Give me a heart quick to confess. Amen.
